subject: Privatenet deployment readiness: punchlist & next steps
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Susan Blake <s.blake@openbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Privatenet deployment readiness: punchlist & next steps

Susan — thanks for taking time today. Quick recap and the immediate asks so we can get your Private VPC onboarding moving: 

Decisions from call (recap)
- You indicated preference for a Private VPC (PrivateLink preferred over peering where possible due to corporate network policy).
- Goal: staging connectivity in mid-July, production by end of July if procurement and netops align.

Open items / action punchlist (items we'll own vs what we need from OpenBank)
1) Egress IPs: Redwood to provide egress IP list (or optional per-tenant static IPs). ACTION: Redwood to send initial IP pool. (attachment)
2) PrivateLink vs Peering: confirm preferred connectivity type. If PrivateLink, OpenBank needs to approve the VPC endpoint connection; if peering, we'll need route and CIDR assignment. ACTION: OpenBank to confirm network preference and any constraints.
3) Allowlist ports & health-checks: we'll share minimal port list for allowlisting (TLS 443 + health probe ports). ACTION: Redwood to send file with ports.
4) TLS & certs: clarify whether OpenBank will terminate TLS at their edge or we should present certs. ACTION: OpenBank to confirm termination model.
5) KMS / key management: you flagged requirement for KMS integration for at-rest encryption keys in Private deployments. ACTION: Redwood to outline KMS options and needed IAM roles.
6) Compliance artifacts: request for SOC2 / security questionnaire follow-up. ACTION: OpenBank security will send questionnaire; Redwood to respond.

Next steps
- I'm attaching a one-page punchlist (redwood_privatenet_punchlist_v1.xlsx) — internal/NetOps checklist.
- Can we schedule a NetOps technical working session next week (proposed: Thu 6/16 or Fri 6/17)? Please share the best contact on your side for firewall/allowlist work.

If anything is missing from my recap, flag it and I'll update. I'll follow up with the IP list and a short allowlist/ports file from Aditya.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Susan Blake <s.blake@openbank.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Jenkins <mark.jenkins@openbank.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Privatenet deployment readiness: punchlist & next steps

Connor — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few things from our side: 

- We are proceeding with a Private VPC. PrivateLink is preferred because our security team wants minimal route propagation and tighter control over ingress.
- NetOps contact: Mark Jenkins (mark.jenkins@openbank.com) — he will own allowlisting and peering approvals.
- Timeline: mid-July for staging looks realistic, subject to procurement and our change window approvals.

A few clarifying Qs:
1) Can Redwood provide a set of egress IPs that we can allowlist, or will we need to provision static NAT IPs in our VPC to ensure traffic egresses from fixed addresses? We prefer Redwood-provided static IPs if possible.
2) We will need SOC2 evidence and a short summary of what audit logs are available for Private deployments.

I'll review the punchlist and share it with Mark. Please include the expected owner for each item (Redwood vs OpenBank) in the punchlist.

Thanks — Susan
Susan Blake
Director, Cloud Operations | OpenBank
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Susan Blake <s.blake@openbank.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Privatenet deployment readiness: punchlist & next steps

Susan / Mark — looping in a couple of technical clarifications and attachments to help NetOps scope the work quickly.

Short answers first: 
- Redwood supports two common egress patterns for Private VPC: (A) Shared Redwood-managed egress IP pool (we announce a small set of static IPs you can allowlist), or (B) Customer-managed per-tenant static IPs (NAT in your VPC) — option B is supported but involves extra configuration and a reserved cost.
- For PrivateLink there's a consumer approval step on your side; we provide the endpoint service name and the ARN for AWS (or equivalent in Azure/GCP).
- Required ports: outbound TLS 443 to our endpoint(s) plus ICMP for path MTU checks and an ephemeral range for health checks. I attached a CSV with the recommended egress IPs to get you started.

Attachments included: redwood_egress_ips_v1.csv (sample IP blocks), redwood_privatenet_punchlist_v1.xlsx (owner column filled where immediate), egress_ports.txt (minimal port set).

Proposed NetOps sync: Thu 2028-06-16 09:00 PT or Fri 2028-06-17 11:00 PT. Please confirm which works for Mark.

Connor: I flagged items in the punchlist where we request documents (SOC2, encryption design). I can draft the KMS/IAM snippet we need from OpenBank as soon as Mark confirms the team.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success / Solutions | Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Mark Jenkins <mark.jenkins@openbank.com>, Susan Blake <s.blake@openbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Privatenet deployment readiness: punchlist & next steps

Mark / Susan — quick technical note to add to the punchlist before the NetOps call: 

- Ports: primary requirement is outbound 443 (TLS) to our PrivateLink endpoint or to our egress IPs if you're using peering. Health-checks from Redwood will originate from the same IP pool; no inbound ports to your app are required for normal traffic.
- If you route via a corporate HTTP proxy, we'll need the proxy host/port and any mTLS requirements.
- PrivateLink: from a consumer perspective you simply accept the endpoint connection; we will provide the service name and attestations for the endpoint.

I attached a tiny file with the port list and a short note on NAT patterns (egress_ports.txt). Happy to go deeper on the call.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Susan Blake <s.blake@openbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Privatenet deployment readiness: punchlist & next steps

Thanks, all — Mark and I reviewed the attachments. A couple of quick confirms: 

- NetOps is available Thu 6/16 09:00 PT for the sync. Mark will join and I'll have our security lead on the bridge for questionnaire items.
- We prefer the Redwood-managed egress IP pool if possible; please confirm whether a small block (eg a /29 or /28) can be reserved per account, and share any pricing for per-tenant static IPs as an alternative.
- Please send the SOC2 pack and a short note about what audit logs we can expect to ingest or export.

We'll be prepared to accept a PrivateLink connection during the call if everything looks good. Thanks for getting the punchlist together — we'll aim to close this milestone quickly.

Regards,
Susan Blake
Director, Cloud Operations | OpenBank
